hypothesis: Eggs ('nits') of lice, fleas, and bedbugs do not develop into any further stage.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. SUPPORTS only if the Animal Diversity Web accounts of Pediculus humanus, Pulex irritans, and Cimex lectularius each state that the eggs do not hatch or generate no offspring.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if at least one of the three accounts states that eggs hatch into a nymph, larva, or other immature stage. MIXED if at least one account states that eggs do not develop further and at least one states that they hatch. INCONCLUSIVE with reason data-unavailable if none of the three accounts can be fetched or none states either outcome; reason underpowered is not used, because one explicit hatching statement refutes the universal. GBIF lifeStage facet counts are recorded and do not decide the verdict: nymph or adult occurrences do not by themselves prove that those eggs hatched.

test_contract.expected_observation: Life-cycle prose for the human louse, a flea, and the bedbug says their eggs produce nothing further.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Life-cycle prose says the eggs of at least one of those insects hatch into a nymph or larva.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public species accounts that describe development, plus GBIF occurrence lifeStage facets as a non-decisive count. The three taxa are fixed: Pediculus humanus, Pulex irritans, Cimex lectularius.
test_contract.inference_method: Strip HTML and match sentences. A hatch statement is a sentence containing egg or nit and hatch, nymph, or larva. A terminal statement is a sentence containing egg or nit and a phrase that nothing further is produced or that eggs do not hatch. The universal is refuted by one hatch statement and supported only if all three accounts are terminal.

interpretation: Aristotle's 'nits' are read as the eggs of lice, fleas, and bugs (bedbugs, Cimex), which is the scope recorded for this claim. 'Generate nothing' is read as the eggs not developing into a later conspecific stage. Producing a nit is not in dispute; only whether the nit develops.

datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web accounts of Pediculus humanus, Pulex irritans, and Cimex lectularius
datasets.role: life-cycle prose for the three named insects

datasets.name: GBIF lifeStage facets for the same three taxa
datasets.role: non-decisive counts of recorded life stages

method: HTML was stripped and cut before the ADW glossary. A sentence matches hatching when it joins egg or nit with hatch, nymph, or larva. A sentence matches a terminal egg when it says eggs do not hatch or generate nothing. One hatching account refutes the universal. GBIF lifeStage facets were stored and not used for the verdict.

measured.unit: of three taxa whose account says the eggs hatch

hatch_sentences: The nits will hatch into nymphs in about eight days.
Eggs, larvae and pupae are usually also found in the immediate habitat of the host, if not on the host.
The eggs hatch about four to six days later.

headline: Louse nits are described as hatching into nymphs, and flea eggs as hatching, so those eggs do not generate nothing.
caveats: The Cimex lectularius ADW URL is a classification stub with no life-cycle prose. One hatching account is enough to refute the universal.
GBIF life-stage counts do not show that a particular nit hatched. They are not part of the verdict.
The louse interval 'about eight days' and the flea interval are in the fetched sentences stored in measured.extra.
